pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

- generate and display backup codes during 2fa setup
- enable their use during 2fa login flow
- fix 2fa setup test to include new backup code screen

[backup-codes-setup.webm](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/assets/55853254/3bebfb21-f7ef-4717-9135-ac30387cfb18)

[backup-codes-login.webm](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/assets/55853254/71ef61b1-af6f-4e32-bf1e-455e52560535)

Fixes #9910
/claim #9910

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## How should this be tested?

1. Setup 2fa to see the generated backup codes
2. Try to login with them by clicking on "Lost access"

## Mandatory Tasks

- [x] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
pr.title: feat: 2fa backup codes

raw_findings.body: The new backup-code component reports itself as "TwoFactor", colliding with the real TwoFactor component (apps/web/components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx) and making debugging/maintenance misleading.
raw_findings.evidence: export default function TwoFactor({ center = true }) {
raw_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability/readability degradation; misleading component identity in tooling.
raw_findings.impact: The new backup-code component reports itself as "TwoFactor", colliding with the real TwoFactor component (apps/web/components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx) and making debugging/maintenance misleading.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new file was copied from TwoFactor.tsx and the function identifier was not renamed.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the exported function to `BackupCode` to match the file name and its actual responsibility.
raw_findings.title: BackupCode component is exported under the name TwoFactor
raw_findings.trigger: Any developer inspecting the backup-code UI in React DevTools, stack traces, or grepping for the component definition in BackupCode.tsx.

raw_findings.body: The created object URL (and its underlying blob) is retained for the lifetime of the document instead of being released; it is only revoked on a subsequent setup call.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Resource (blob/object URL) leak within the browser session.
raw_findings.impact: The created object URL (and its underlying blob) is retained for the lifetime of the document instead of being released; it is only revoked on a subsequent setup call.
raw_findings.root_cause: resetState() clears password/error/step but does not revoke the object URL created during setup.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Call URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl) inside resetState() (or a cleanup effect on unmount) and clear the backupCodesUrl/backupCodes state.
raw_findings.title: Object URL for backup codes download is leaked when modal is closed
raw_findings.trigger: User completes 2FA setup (creating a blob URL) and then closes the dialog via the close/cancel buttons, which call resetState() that never revokes backupCodesUrl.

raw_findings.body: The core new feature paths (authorize() backup-code branch in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts backup-code branch) can regress silently without any failing test.
raw_findings.evidence: // TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup
raw_findings.failure_mode: Introduced feature logic is unverified, allowing undetected regressions.
raw_findings.impact: The core new feature paths (authorize() backup-code branch in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts backup-code branch) can regress silently without any failing test.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only UI-presentation of backup codes was tested; the authentication logic was left untested and explicitly deferred via TODO.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add e2e steps that decrypt a generated backup code, use it via the "Lost access" flow to log in, and to disable 2FA, asserting success and single-use invalidation.
raw_findings.title: New backup-code login/disable flow has no automated test coverage
raw_findings.trigger: Running the 2FA e2e suite: it only exercises the display/download/copy/close of backup codes, never actually logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code.
